fields.h1: Build a Conjoint Survey That Shows What People Trade Off
fields.hero_description: Build a conjoint survey that shows people product profiles side by side and counts which features win their choices.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into Each Choice Task
fields.features_subheading: Describe the product and the parts that can vary. Emergent builds the tasks, a table of every pick, and a dashboard of choice rates.
fields.feature_1:
Choice tasks built from your attributes

Name each attribute and its levels, like price at $16, $20 or $24. Emergent builds choice tasks that show a few product profiles per screen and ask which one the person would pick.
fields.feature_2:
A fresh mix of profiles for each person

Each respondent sees fresh profiles mixed from your levels, every level shown about as often as the rest. Tell Emergent which levels may never meet, like the top price with no perks.
fields.feature_3:
A none option when walking away is real

Add a none of these choice where a buyer could keep their current plan or buy nothing. Each none pick is saved like any other answer and shows how often no profile was good enough.
fields.feature_4:
Choice rates per level on a dashboard

The dashboard shows how often each level was chosen out of the times it was shown. A follow-up prompt adds a split, such as new subscribers against those of two years or more.
fields.feature_5:
One task per screen, no cap on responses

People answer one choice task per screen and tap a profile to move on, which fits a phone. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and the study can go to every customer on your list.
fields.feature_6:
Every pick in a database you own

Each choice is a row in a database you own, with the profiles shown and the one picked. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run the study next year.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Decisions Made From Choice Tasks
fields.tab_content_1:
Free shipping outweighed $4 more for each bag

Orrinsby Roasters was weighing a price rise for its coffee subscription. It asked 420 subscribers 10 choice tasks, each showing 3 plans that mixed price, bag size, and shipping. Free shipping raised a plan's choice rate by 19 points, and $4 more a bag cut it by 15. The roaster moved to $20 a bag with free shipping.
fields.tab_content_2:
With reply drafts in it, a plan won more picks

Velbrook's product team had room for one more feature in the Pro plan of its help desk software. Each of 280 account admins picked between 3 plan versions in 8 tasks. Plans with reply drafts were chosen 27 points more often, and phone support added 5. The team posted the result in Slack and put reply drafts in Pro.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two remote days each week beat a bigger match

Dunmerrow Freight put the study on employees' phones: 12 tasks, each a pair of packages mixing remote days, paid time off, and the 401(k) match. Of 640 employees, 512 finished. Packages with 2 remote days a week won 42 points more often, and the higher match added 10. The HR director got the summary by email.
fields.tab_content_4:
To riders, waiting cost more than a higher fare

Quorrel Valley Transit could afford one change on Route 7. It asked 900 riders 9 choice tasks, each comparing 3 versions of the route by frequency, walk to the stop, and fare. Frequency moved the choice rate by 31 points from best level to worst, the walk by 11, and the fare by 6. The board chose a bus every 10 minutes.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Conjoint Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps that turn a pricing or feature question into a conjoint survey people can finish on a phone.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep it to six attributes or fewer
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set how many tasks each person sees
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the one call the study will settle, such as the price of a new plan or which feature goes into Pro. Every attribute should bear on that call. Put the decision in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the attributes around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List the parts of the offer that can change, like contract length and support hours. Sawtooth Software describes this as breaking the product into its components. Six or fewer keeps every profile readable on one phone screen.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write levels a buyer could actually face, like $16, $20 and $24 a bag rather than $5 and $50. Use the same unit across levels, and keep each attribute to 2 to 4 of them. Every extra level needs more respondents to count.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Sawtooth Software puts the usual count between 8 and 20 choice tasks per respondent. Start near 10, with 3 profiles in each, and time yourself on a phone. If it runs long, cut tasks before you cut attributes.
fields.howto_step_5_des: If staying with what they have now is a real option for buyers, offer none of these in every task. Without it, the study tells you which profile wins against the others, not whether anyone would buy any of them.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sawtooth Software calls 300 respondents a good rule of thumb for sample size, and its formula aims for at least 500 appearances per level. Count your levels and tasks first, since a study with many levels needs more people.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the choice rates, then the swings
fields.howto_step_7_des: Compare each level with the other levels of its own attribute, then compare the swing between attributes. For part-worth utilities, pull the raw choices from your database into a statistics tool. Split by group only where each group is large.

faq_plan.q: What is a conjoint in a survey?
faq_plan.ref: What is a conjoint in a survey?

prov.original: What is a conjoint in a survey?

faq_plan.a: A conjoint is a block of choice tasks inside a survey: each task shows a few product profiles that mix levels such as price and features, and the person picks one. Sawtooth Software describes conjoint analysis as a quantitative marketing research method that is popular for product and pricing research. A conjoint survey is the questionnaire that collects those picks.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a conjoint survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the decision, the attributes and their levels in Emergent's AI survey builder, and say how many tasks and profiles each person sees. Emergent builds the choice tasks and the database behind them. Take the survey on a phone yourself, change anything by prompt, and publish once every task reads clearly.

faq_plan.q: Can you give me an example of a conjoint survey?
faq_plan.ref: Can you give me an example of a conjoint survey?

prov.original: Can you give me an example of a conjoint survey?

faq_plan.a: Yes. A gym testing memberships could vary the monthly price ($30, $40, or $50), class access, and contract length. Each member sees 10 tasks of 3 memberships and picks one per task. The choice rates then show whether unlimited classes are worth $10 more a month to the people who would pay it.

faq_plan.q: Can a conjoint survey test features of a video game?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A studio can vary the price, the game modes and the length of the campaign, and players pick the version they would buy. Run it apart from your game survey questions about play experience, which ask what players think of a game they already own.

faq_plan.q: How is a choice-based conjoint survey different from a rating-based one?
faq_plan.a: In choice-based conjoint, people pick one profile from a set, as a buyer does at a shelf. Sawtooth Software notes that in that method the respondent expresses preferences by choosing from sets of concepts, rather than rating or ranking them. Rating-based studies ask for a score on each profile instead.

faq_plan.q: Should a conjoint survey include price as an attribute?
faq_plan.a: Include price when the decision touches price, and set the levels at amounts you would really charge. With price in the study, you can set a feature's pull against a price step, such as free shipping against $4 more. Leave it out when price is fixed and only the features are in question.

faq_plan.q: What should I ask before the choice tasks in a conjoint survey?
faq_plan.a: Ask only what you need to qualify people and split the results later, such as their current plan or how often they buy. Two or three audience survey questions are enough. Put them first, so anyone outside your market leaves before the tasks begin.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep a conjoint survey from feeling repetitive?
faq_plan.a: Show a progress line such as task 4 of 10, keep each profile short, and use the same layout in every task so people compare instead of reread. In an app Emergent builds, the survey runs as a conversational flow with one task per screen.

faq_plan.q: How do I test a conjoint survey before sending it?
faq_plan.a: Send it to 10 or 20 colleagues first. Check that every level turns up, that no profile beats another on every attribute, and how long a phone takes. Each pilot answer lands in a database you own, so you can count how often each level was shown before launch.

faq_plan.q: Can a conjoint survey help choose a training program?
faq_plan.a: It fits when you are choosing how to run the program. Vary the format, the length, and the time of day, and let employees pick the version they would sign up for. Emergent builds the tasks from a prompt and changes them by prompt for a second round. That differs from learning and development survey questions, which ask which skills people want to build.

plan.angle: The top 10 is definitions and analysis guides from research-software vendors and journals: they explain attributes, levels and part-worths but never show a finished study end to end. This page shows four choice-based conjoint surveys built from a prompt, each ending in a pricing, packaging, benefits or service decision read from choice rates, and the how-to covers attribute limits, task counts, the none option and sample size with sourced rules of thumb.
tab_stories: Orrinsby Roasters asks 420 coffee subscribers 10 choice tasks of 3 plans each, finds free shipping lifts the choice rate 19 points while a $4 price rise costs 15, and moves to a $20 plan with free shipping.

Velbrook's product team sends 280 help desk admins 8 choice tasks, reply drafts lift a plan from 20% to 47% while phone support moves it from 31% to 36%, and the team posts the result in Slack and puts reply drafts in the Pro plan.

Dunmerrow Freight asks 640 employees to pick between 2 benefit packages in 12 tasks on their phones, 2 remote days a week win 71% of the time against a 6% match at 55%, and the HR director gets the summary by email.

Quorrel Valley Transit asks 900 riders 6 choice tasks about bus service, frequency swings the choice rate by 31 points against 11 for walking distance and 6 for the fare, and the board runs Route 7 every 10 minutes.
